plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked schematic and scale comparison shows Walter Brattain and John Bardeen's 16 December 1947 point-contact transistor (two gold-foil contacts separated by 1/500th inch = ~0.005 cm on n-type germanium, amplifying power ~18× to 100×) alongside William Shockley's January 1948 three-layer junction transistor and Jack Kilby (12 September 1958) & Robert Noyce's (23 January 1959) monolithic integrated circuit vs 1946 ENIAC (17,468 tubes, 30 tonnes, 150 kW) and a modern chip (>15 billion switches).

teach_overlay.label: 1946 ENIAC (17,468 TUBES, 30 T) VS 1947 GERMPANIUM WEDGE VS >15B CHIP
teach_overlay.detail: Inked schematic & scale chart on period paper comparing 1946 ENIAC (17,468 glass tubes, 30 tonnes, 150 kW), 16 Dec 1947 point-contact transistor (0.005 cm razor-slit gold gap on germanium), and a fingernail silicon chip (>15 billion transistors)
teach_overlay.scale: 17,468 glass tubes filling a room and gulping enough power for a hundred homes — replaced today by 15 billion crystal switches on a chip the size of your fingernail
